raw_segments.text: Whether I really had been down in Garden Court in the dead of the night, groping about
for the boat that I supposed to be there. Whether I had two or three times come to myself
on the staircase with great terror, not knowing how I had got out of bed. Whether I had found
myself lighting the lamp, possessed by the idea that he was coming up the stairs, and
that the lights were blown out. Whether I had been inexpressibly harassed by the distracted
talking, laughing, and groaning of someone, and had half suspected those sounds to be
of my own making. Whether there had been a closed iron furnace in a dark corner of the
room, and a voice had called out, over and over again, that Miss Havisham was consuming
within it. These were things that I tried to settle with myself and get into some order,
as I lay that morning on my bed. But the vapor of a lime kiln would come between
me and them, disordering them all, and it was through the vapor at last that I saw two
men looking at me.
